atom:entry.atom:title: code-review-mcp-server: Command injection via unsanitized folderPath/baseBranch parameters
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: HIGH
Summary: ### Impact `code-review-mcp-server` exposes MCP tools (`getLocalGitDiff`, `codeReview`, `createPR`, `getPRTemplate`) that accept `folderPath` and `baseBranch` string parameters. These caller-controlled values were interpolated directly into shell command strings executed via `child_process.execSync()`, which runs commands through `/bin/sh`. A crafted value such as `baseBranch = "main; <arbitrary command> #"` (or a `$(...)` command substitution, or a `folderPath` that breaks out of the surrounding quotes) results in **arbitrary command execution** on the host running the MCP server. ### Patches Fixed in **1.5.3**. Every `execSync()` call was replaced with `execFileSync()` using argument arrays, so inputs are passed directly to `git` / `gh` without going through a shell, eliminating the injection at its root. ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to `code-review-mcp-server@1.5.3` or later.
Suggested next step: Check whether affected package versions are present in your dependencies and review the maintainer's fix guidance.
Original advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jq3q-62jc-fqq9
Watchlist match only. Local exposure has not been assessed.

atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.8 (v3.1)

atom:entry.atom:title: Apache Pyfory python is vulnerable to deserialization of untrusted data
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.8 (v3.1)
Summary: Deserialization of untrusted data in python in pyfory versions 0.12.0 through 0.12.2, or the legacy pyfury versions from 0.1.0 through 0.10.3: allows arbitrary code execution. An application is vulnerable if it reads pyfory serialized data from untrusted sources. An attacker can craft a data stream that selects pickle-fallback serializer during deserialization, leading to the execution of `pickle.loads`, which is vulnerable to remote code execution. Users are recommended to upgrade to pyfory version 0.12.3 or later, which has removed pickle fallback serializer and thus fixes this issue.

atom:entry.atom:title: PraisonAI MCP `tools/call` path-traversal => RCE via Python `.pth` injection

atom:entry.atom:title: Remote code execution in pytorch lightning
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.8 (v3.0)
Summary: A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability exists in the lightning-ai/pytorch-lightning library version 2.2.1 due to improper handling of deserialized user input and mismanagement of dunder attributes by the `deepdiff` library. The library uses `deepdiff.Delta` objects to modify application state based on frontend actions. However, it is possible to bypass the intended restrictions on modifying dunder attributes, allowing an attacker to construct a serialized delta that passes the deserializer whitelist and contains dunder attributes. When processed, this can be exploited to access other modules, classes, and instances, leading to arbitrary attribute write and total RCE on any self-hosted pytorch-lightning application in its default configuration, as the delta endpoint is enabled by default.

atom:entry.atom:title: AIOHTTP: WebSocket max_msg_size bypass via integer overflow
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 7.5 (v3.1)
Summary: ### Summary The `max_msg_size` check in the WebSocket reader added the declared frame length to the size of the partial message already buffered. In the C extension this addition is 64-bit arithmetic, so a declared length close to 2**63 overflowed and the check passed. ### Impact An attacker could bypass `max_msg_size` and cause unbounded memory use by streaming an oversized WebSocket message after a small non-final fragment. ### Workaround If unable to upgrade, the Python reader is unaffected and can be used with `AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS=1`. --- Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/8cfbe9abe5e11b84006a10f9bdf82bf607671dab

atom:entry.atom:title: AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request replay and buffer growth behind a declined upgrade
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: HIGH / CVSS 8.2 (v3.1)
Summary: ### Summary When the pipelined request queue was full, the pure-Python parser stored the unparsed remainder internally and also returned it to the caller. After a handler declined an upgrade request, the buffered data was re-fed, so the buffer grew with each handled request and already-handled requests were dispatched to the application again. ### Impact If users are using the Python parser (`AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS`, or not a standard wheel installed), an attacker could cause excessive memory use and cause pipelined requests to be processed more than once. ### Workaround Switch to the default C parser. --- Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/47babd8c23ca79e2bae6cc8dcb5752b61e369fc7
